title: Adaptive Honest Intervals for a Median Located at a Density Minimum
banked_reason: Orujov2026 is an acknowledged closest anti-mode/percentile neighbor, but its theorem text and assumptions remain unavailable, so field-level novelty relative to its precise results cannot yet be supported.
gap_reasons: Orujov2026 is an acknowledged closest anti-mode/percentile neighbor, but its theorem text and assumptions remain unavailable, so field-level novelty relative to its precise results cannot yet be supported.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery narrowed the original causal-QTE proposal to a κ=2 fixed-known-quantile density-minimum problem with a concrete three-regime expected-length frontier, same-floor Hellinger pair, and adaptive selector obligations. The proposal did not reach derivation: two Stage D-0.5 reviews repeated the same field-novelty defect because the closest Orujov (2026) theorem text was lawfully inaccessible. The mathematics remains a plausible subfield re-raise once a theorem-level comparator audit can establish a non-overlapping novelty delta.
tldr: Can one honest interval locate a fixed median that is also the unique linearly isolated minimum of its density when the minimum height is unknown? The tentative answer is a joint rank-and-shape expected-length frontier with three floor regimes, attained by one floor-free interval. Resolving it would show when the median rank or the density valley controls precision; known-propensity QTE inference follows by exact thinning and interval differences.
gap: Generic quantile intervals use rank but not minimum shape, while extremum methods use shape but not the known quantile rank. The interaction forces a remote mass correction in same-floor lower alternatives and may create a second crossover.
fill: Prove or refute the fixed-constant \(\kappa=2\) same-floor minimax rate, build a single uniformly honest adaptive interval, and establish legal rank-preserving lower experiments; then transfer the iid theorem to known-propensity QTEs as a corollary.
